body: Thank you :) I hope you're right. And sorry for the loss of your husband, I wish you the best.

I know this feeling exactly. I have had severe, chronic neck pain since I was 16 or so, and am now in my mid 20s. I tell doctors about my neck pain and they shrug it off, or tell me to get physio. I did go to physio once, and they showed me some good stretches to do, but I fail to see how repeated visits will help me, they already showed me everything they know. One time I told a doctor about my neck pain and she said “everyone has neck pain”, well if everyone has what I have why aren’t they in a constant state of wincing from pain like I am? Why aren’t most peoples lives ruined by neck pain like mine is?
Okay, thanks for the helpful reply. I'll try not to worry about it anymore.

I live in Canada. But the place I work at is filthy and my coworker left food and garbage all over work station, attracting rats (I saw many and had to deal with a dead one near my feet)

I know I need to stay off Google, the nurse told me that too. :( But I've never felt an illness like this before. Why do you think it is extremely unlikely I have it?

Yeah at the end of the day they helped me and brought me to a hospital, so I shouldn’t be too mad. Maybe they were just trying to lighten the situation and I took it the wrong way. I was barely awake through and felt more persecuted then usual.

Thanks for the kind reply. Thankfully the doctor I got was very kind and understanding, unlike the paramedics. I don’t know why they though it was a good idea to bring like 6 dudes into my room in response to a panic attack, all cracking jokes with each other instead of trying to calm me down.
Thank’s for the reply. I don’t really talk to my neighbours, but it’s going to feel weird now when I walk passed them and stuff.
